_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `Block5dMutation` is a semio-NATIVE vocabulary carried in `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio`, so no oracle is registered and the decision below records what stands in for one.

oracles.rationale: A second implementation of the `s.block.5d` part-kind document and all forty-one typed mutations, in Python, at `../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-block-5d-1/🐍️component.py`. Written from `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🔣️component.json` (the thirteen members), `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/🔣️component.json` (the forty-one verbs and their argument lists), rules 1, 2 and 7 of `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️12/SEMANTIC-MUTATIONS-OVERHAUL/📓️derivation-rules.md`, and the forty-one committed `(before, mutation, diff, outcome, after)` quintets — which are the only statement of the one thing this vocabulary does not share with its siblings: that `update-part2d` REBUILDS the 2d facet from its six arguments in their declared order and DROPS every member whose argument is null, turning a `{shape, radius, color, iconKind}` circle into a `{shape, width, height, color}` rectangle. It imports nothing from this repository and transliterates none of its Rust. This registration SUPERSEDES the `block-5d-mutation-semantics` no-oracle decision, whose argument — that the `2d`/`3d` to `part2d`/`part3d` diff renaming "IS this subset's specification, not a fact an external library could confirm or refute" — was already refuted by the sibling `mutate-block-2d-1`, which took a Python second implementation over the same carrier in the same plugin; a renaming is something a second implementation resolves through a declared alias table, which is exactly what this one does. All forty-one kinds are adjudicated and none is refused: unlike its `🧊️3d` sibling this subset holds its whole grip-kind vocabulary locally, so no verb reaches a composed child whose id is content-addressed by an unstated function. ONE CEILING ON WHAT THIS COMPARISON ESTABLISHES, stated rather than implied: the SUBJECT half of this case does not run this subset's codec — `../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-block-5d-1/🦀️component.rs` links no plugin crate and replays the committed vectors — so today the comparison establishes that an independent implementation of the specification computes the committed after-snapshots, which is a real check of the vectors and the class of check that found `mutate-jack-1`'s wrong vector, but not yet our codec against a second producer. A `block5d_mutation_report_json` bridge beside the mutation enum, the one thing `mutate-block-2d-1` gained in this wave, is what closes it; it is not added here because `semio-s-plugin-block` does not compile today (1,522 errors from a peer session's in-flight async refactor), so it could not be verified. This case also reads no real-world artifact: all 205 of its fixtures are handcrafted specification vectors. `package` is deliberately empty: the implementation needs no distribution, so this entry contributes nothing to `🔒️dependencies.json`.
